scope: The standing Dragon Pavilion hall in Kaifeng, including its elevated masonry platform, double glazed roof, 72-step approach and carved central ramp.

references.caption: Oblique view shows the raised red-faced base, narrower stone stairs and the terrace balustrade. The double-eaved roof has golden tile, gable shoulders, turned-up corners, red posts and wide lower eaves.

originalReview.notes: Oblique view shows the raised red-faced base, narrower stone stairs and the terrace balustrade. The double-eaved roof has golden tile, gable shoulders, turned-up corners, red posts and wide lower eaves.

references.caption: Straight view confirms the symmetry of the upper hall, shape of both roofs, position and width of the central carved ramp and parallel stair runs, and masonry shoulders.

references.caption: View from the stairs shows the carved imperial dragon ramp, stone baluster caps and pierced panels, deep eaves and the gold-on-dark pavilion name under the upper roof.
